2. For U2 (configurable logging directory): The log directory will be configured via a new externalized Spring property `xd.log.dir`, with the existing `${xd.home}/logs` path retained as the default value to maintain backward compatibility.
3. For U3 (move message-bus to spring-bus): The extracted message-bus code will be packaged as a standalone `spring-bus` Maven module with no dependencies on Spring XD-specific code, and will include Spring Boot auto-configuration for ease of use in other projects.
4. For U4 (move type conversion to spring-cloud-dataflow): The extracted type conversion logic will be added to the `spring-cloud-dataflow-common` module to be accessible to both the Spring Cloud Data Flow server and custom module implementations, with no breaking changes to existing public APIs.
5. For U5 (move serialization codec to spring-bus): The serialization codec will be integrated into the `spring-bus` module to be shared across all bus communication, with backward-compatible message format support to avoid breaking existing deployments.
6. For U6 (singlenode XD Admin SPI): The singlenode implementation will reuse the existing Module Launcher SPI from Spring XD, running both the admin container and module containers in the same JVM with local file system-based artifact storage for simplicity.

technical_and_design_decisions: For U1 (Teradata Sqoop NPE fix): The root cause is missing default connection manager configuration for Teradata JDBC URLs in the Spring XD Sqoop module. The fix integrates the Hortonworks Teradata connector as a default dependency and adds automatic detection of Teradata JDBC URLs to apply the correct connection manager without user intervention.

For U2 (configurable logging directory): The log directory is configured via a new externalized Spring property `xd.log.dir`, with the existing `${xd.home}/logs` path retained as the default value to maintain backward compatibility.

For U3 (move message-bus to spring-bus): The extracted message-bus code is packaged as a standalone `spring-bus` Maven module with no dependencies on Spring XD-specific code, and includes Spring Boot auto-configuration for ease of use in other projects.

For U4 (move type conversion to spring-cloud-dataflow): The extracted type conversion logic is added to the `spring-cloud-dataflow-common` module to be accessible to both the Spring Cloud Data Flow server and custom module implementations, with no breaking changes to existing public APIs.

For U5 (move serialization codec to spring-bus): The serialization codec is integrated into the `spring-bus` module to be shared across all bus communication, with backward-compatible message format support to avoid breaking existing deployments.

For U6 (singlenode XD Admin SPI): The singlenode implementation reuses the existing Module Launcher SPI from Spring XD, running both the admin container and module containers in the same JVM with local file system-based artifact storage for simplicity.

For U7 (Diego Receptor XD Admin SPI): The Diego implementation uses the official Cloud Foundry Diego Receptor Java client, and supports both Lattice and Diego runtime environments with minimal configuration changes.

For U8 (s-c-s module self-registration): Module self-registration uses Spring Cloud's service discovery abstractions (supporting Eureka, Consul, etc.) and is opt-in via a simple configuration property to avoid impacting existing modules that do not require service discovery.
